title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Incident Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Comms Templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response process. It covers severity definitions, roles and responsibilities, triage and mitigation workflows, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and escalation, game day guidance, and customer-facing status page / communications templates. The goal is consistent, fast, and accountable incident handling with clear follow-up to prevent recurrence.

Scope

- Applies to production-facing services across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Owners: engineering (primary), eng-sre (operational lead), customer-success (external comms).

Severity levels and thresholds

1) Sev 1 — Platform outage / customer impact (P0)
   - Symptoms: Regional or global API failures, >30% of requests failing or majority of customers impacted.
   - Thresholds: error rate > 10% sustained for 5 minutes OR median p95 latency > 5s on inference-gateway affecting >50% traffic.
   - SLO impact: immediate breach of availability SLO (99.9% monthly).

2) Sev 2 — Major degradation (P1)
   - Symptoms: Significant performance degradation or partial feature outage affecting a subset of customers.
   - Thresholds: error rate 1%-10% sustained for 10 minutes OR p95 latency > 2s for a critical route.

3) Sev 3 — Minor degradation (P2)
   - Symptoms: Non-critical errors, intermittent throttling, or performance regressions for a small percentage of traffic.

4) Sev 4 — Informational / no customer impact (P3)
   - Symptoms: Internal alerts, developer impact, or scheduled maintenance.

Roles & responsibilities

- Pager (First responder): Acknowledges page within configured SLA (2 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2).
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns cross-team coordination until handoff; assigns roles (scribe, communications).
- Scribe: Documents timeline and actions in the incident doc.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners (runtime, gateway, kv-cache, orchestration).
- Eng-SRE: Provides runbook guidance, escalations to infra, and system-level mitigations.
- Customer Success: Owns customer-facing updates and post-incident outreach for impacted customers.

Pager and escalation policy

- Paging platform: PagerDuty integration via service-specific PD services (e.g., inference-gateway-pd).
- Primary rotation: 1-week primary on-call, 2-week secondary.
- Acknowledgement: Primary must acknowledge Sev1 within 2 minutes; if no ack, escalate to secondary after 5 minutes, then to oncall-lead after 15 minutes.

Incident lifecycle (high level)

1) Detect & Alert
   - Alerts should include: service, metric threshold breached, link to dashboard, last 15m trend, suggested urgency.
2) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Pager acknowledges, determines scope (global/regional/customer-impact), and assigns severity.
3) Mitigate (10-60 minutes)
   - Execute runbook steps, apply mitigations, enable fallbacks (route to healthy region/model variant).
4) Stabilize (60-240 minutes)
   - Restore traffic, confirm SLOs returning to normal, prepare customer comms.
5) Resolve & Close (post-stabilization)
   - Create incident postmortem, list action items with owners and due dates, and schedule follow-ups.

Runbook template (copy into service repo and link here)

- Title: short service + symptom (e.g., inference-gateway - 502 spike)
- Pager: PagerDuty service name and escalation policy
- Ownership: primary on-call team, primary SME
- Quick diagnosis checklist (5 bullets)
- Immediate mitigations (ordered steps)
- Escalation steps and contacts (Slack channels and pager handles)
- Recovery verification (commands and dashboards)
- Post-incident notes and links

Example runbook table (plain text table recommended for Confluence)

| Item | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Service | inference-gateway |
| Symptom | 502 / 503 spikes for text-generation route |
| Pager | inference-gateway-pd (Escalation: primary->secondary->lead) |
| Quick checks | kubectl get pods -n inference | grep error; check cpu/gpu saturation; check kv-cache hitrate |
| Mitigation steps | 1) Roll back last deployment: kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-gateway -n prod
2) Scale up replica set: kubectl scale deploy/inference-gateway --replicas=6 -n prod
3) Enable fallback variant: update routing policy to model-variant-stable |
| Recovery validation | p95 latency < 500ms for 5 consecutive minutes; errors < 0.5% |

Technical runbook snippets

- Check pods and logs:
  - kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-gateway
  - kubectl -n prod logs deploy/inference-gateway -c gateway --since=10m | tail -n 200
- Check GPU utilization:
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 10
- Traffic routing fallback (CLI example):
  - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","route":"/v1/generate","variant":"model-variant-stable"}'

Communications: internal & external

- Internal channels: #oncall (urgent), #incidents (postmortem discussion), incident-management Google Doc (scribe notes).
- Customer-facing: status.redwoodinference.com (public status page), designated incident template (see below).
- Communication cadence for Sev1: initial notice within 30 minutes, updates every 30-60 minutes until resolved, final resolution + postmortem link within 48 hours.

Status page & customer communication templates

Initial incident template (public)

Title: [Service] - Partial outage affecting customers in {region}
Status: Investigating
Impact: Customers may experience increased errors or latency for {route}.
Detected: {HH:MM UTC}
Next update: in 30-60 minutes
Details: We are investigating reports of elevated error rates for {service}. Our engineering team is actively triaging.

Customer update template (progress)

Status: Identified / Mitigating
Impact: {summary}
Root cause: Under investigation (or brief if known)
Mitigation: {actions taken e.g., rolling back to previous deployment, enabling fallback routing}
ETA to resolution: {estimated time}

Resolved template

Status: Resolved
Impact: Service is restored and metrics are within normal ranges.
Root cause: {short summary}
Follow-up: A postmortem will be published within 48 hours with action items.

Postmortem process & template

- Timeline: Postmortem draft due within 48 hours of resolution. Public postmortem for Sev1/Sev2; internal for Sev3/Sev4.
- Required fields: Title, Severity, Incident start/stop times, Impacted customers/regions, Root cause, Contributing factors, Timeline of events, Mitigations applied, Action items (owner + due date), Lessons learned, Links to runbooks/dashboards.

Postmortem template (short)

Title: {service} — {date} — {sev}
Summary: one-paragraph summary
Timeline: numbered timeline with timestamps and actors
Root cause: succinct cause statement
Contributing factors: bullet list
Action items: numbered list with owner and due date (automated JIRA ticket created)

Sample action-item table

| Action | Owner | Due |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add synthetic test for customer route /v1/health-check | eng-platform | 2026-03-01 |
| Harden fallback routing to auto-enable on 5% error rate | runtime-team | 2026-02-28 |

On-call rotations and scheduling rules

- Primary rotation: weekly Monday 08:00 to next Monday 08:00 local timezone.
- Secondary rotation: bi-weekly.
- Swap process: update PagerDuty on-call schedule and post in #oncall with two-week notice.
- Time off coverage: designate an oncall buddy for each week; on-call lead must approve replacements.

Game days (practice incidents)

- Frequency: quarterly system-level game days and monthly team-level drills.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, test escalation paths, exercise cross-team coordination, and verify status page templates.
- Example scenarios: global model-serving outage, KV cache corruption, control plane partition.
- Success criteria: post-game-day retro with action items closed within 30 days; runbook updates merged within 7 days.

Instrumentation & tooling checklist

- Dashboards: service health (5m error rate, p95 latency, capacity), SLO burn rate dashboard.
- Logs: central ELK/Uploaded logs with retention policy, fast query links in alerts.
- Tracing: distributed traces with request sampling for inference requests.
- Paging: PagerDuty services per critical component; integration with Slack and Zoom for bridge creation.

Operational KPIs & SLAs

- Incident MTTA (time to acknowledge): target < 2 minutes for Sev1, < 15 minutes for Sev2.
- MTTR (time to recovery): target < 1 hour for Sev1 mitigation to stabilization; full RCA and postmortem closed with action items tracked within 14 days.

Compliance & retention

- Postmortems and incident artifacts retained in Confluence for 3 years. Sensitive incidents flagged as Restricted and reviewed with Security/Legal.

Appendix: contact list & useful links

- Slack channels: #oncall, #incidents, #eng-sre
- Pager contacts: inference-gateway-pd, runtime-pd, infra-pd
- Key dashboards: /dashboards/inference/gateway-health, /dashboards/slo/error-rate
- Templates & checklists: copy this page to create service-specific runbooks; update runbook last_updated on any change.
